# 2 Samuel Chapter 21 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 193v–193r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_021_page_001.jpg, 2SA_021_page_002.jpg

---

**21:1** And-there-was a-famine in-[the]-days of-David three years, year after year. And-sought David the-face of-YHWH. And-said YHWH, "To Sha'ul and-to-[the]-house of-the-bloods [ha-damim], because he-killed the-Giv'onim."

**21:2** And-called the-king to-the-Giv'onim and-said to-them — and-the-Giv'onim [were]-not from-[the]-sons of-Yisra'el, but [they were] from-[the]-remnant of-the-Emori, and-[the]-sons of-Yisra'el had-sworn to-them — and-sought Sha'ul to-strike-them in-his-zeal [qin'ah] for-[the]-sons of-Yisra'el and-Yehudah.

**21:3** And-said David to the-Giv'onim, "What shall-I-do for-you, and-with-what shall-I-make-atonement [akapper], that-you-may-bless [the]-inheritance of-YHWH?"

**21:4** And-said to-him the-Giv'onim, "There-is-not to-us silver and-gold with Sha'ul and-with his-house, and-there-is-not to-us a-man to-kill in-Yisra'el." And-he-said, "What [are]-you saying? I-will-do [it] for-you."

**21:5** And-they-said to the-king, "The-man who consumed-us and-who planned [dimmah] against-us — we-were-destroyed from-standing in-all [the]-territory of-Yisra'el —

**21:6** let-there-be-given to-us seven men from-his-sons, and-we-will-hang-them [hoqa'anum] before-YHWH in-Giv'ah of-Sha'ul, [the]-chosen-one [bechir] of-YHWH." And-said the-king, "I will-give [them]."

**21:7** And-spared the-king Mefiboshet son of-Yehonatan son of-Sha'ul, on-account-of [the]-oath of-YHWH that [was] between-them, between David and-between Yehonatan son of-Sha'ul.

**21:8** And-took the-king the-two sons of-Ritspah daughter of-Ayyah whom she-bore to-Sha'ul — Armoni and-Mefiboshet — and-the-five sons of-Mikhal daughter of-Sha'ul whom she-bore to-Adri'el son of-Barzillai the-Mecholati.

**21:9** And-he-gave-them into-[the]-hand of-the-Giv'onim, and-they-hung-them [vayoqi'um] on-the-mountain before YHWH. And-fell [the]-seven of-them together; and-they were-put-to-death in-[the]-days of-harvest, in-[the]-first [days], in-[the]-beginning of-[the]-harvest of-barley [se'orim].

**21:10** And-took Ritspah daughter of-Ayyah the-sackcloth [saq] and-spread-it for-herself upon the-rock, from-[the]-beginning of-harvest until water was-poured upon-them from the-heavens. And-she-did-not allow [the]-bird[s] of-the-heavens to-rest upon-them by-day, and-the-beast[s] of-the-field by-night.

**21:11** And-it-was-told to-David what Ritspah daughter of-Ayyah, [the]-concubine of-Sha'ul, had-done.

**21:12** And-went David and-took the-bones of-Sha'ul and-the-bones of-Yehonatan his-son from the-masters [ba'aley] of-Yavesh Gil'ad, who had-stolen them from-[the]-broad-place [rechovah] of-Bet-Shan, where [the]-Pelishtim had-hung-them on-[the]-day [the]-Pelishtim struck Sha'ul in-the-Gilboa.

**21:13** And-he-brought-up from-there the-bones of-Sha'ul and-the-bones of-Yehonatan his-son, and-they-gathered the-bones of-the-ones-hung [ha-muqa'im].

**21:14** And-they-buried the-bones of-Sha'ul and-Yehonatan his-son in-[the]-land of-Binyamin in-Tsela, in-[the]-tomb of-Qish his-father. And-they-did all that the-king commanded. And-was-entreated [vaye'ater] God for-the-land after this.

**21:15** And-there-was again war to-[the]-Pelishtim with Yisra'el. And-went-down David and-his-servants with-him and-fought the-Pelishtim, and-David grew-weary [vaya'af].

**21:16** And-Yishbi in-Nov [Yishbo be-Nov], who [was] among-[the]-descendants of-the-Rafah [ha-rafah] — and-the-weight of-his-spear [was] three-hundred [shekels] weight of-bronze, and-he [was]-girded [with]-new [armor] — and-he-said to-strike David.

**21:17** And-helped-him Avishai son of-Tseruyah, and-struck the-Pelishti and-killed-him. Then swore the-men of-David to-him, saying, "You-shall-not go-out again with-us to-battle, and-you-shall-not extinguish the-lamp [ner] of-Yisra'el."

**21:18** And-it-was after this, and-there-was again the-war in-Gov with-[the]-Pelishtim. Then struck Sibbekhai the-Chushati Saf, who [was] among-[the]-descendants of-the-Rafah.

**21:19** And-there-was again the-war in-Gov with-[the]-Pelishtim. And-struck Elchanan son of-Ya'arey-Oregim the-Bet-ha-Lachmi [the Bethlehemite] Golyat [Goliath] the-Gitti, and-[the]-shaft of-his-spear [was] like-a-beam of-weavers ['oregim].

**21:20** And-there-was again war in-Gat, and-there-was a-man of-stature [madon/midin], and-[the]-fingers of-his-hands and-[the]-toes of-his-feet [were] six and-six, twenty-four in-number, and-also he was-born to-the-Rafah.

**21:21** And-he-reproached [vayecharef] Yisra'el, and-struck-him Yehonatan son of-Shim'i [Shim'ah] brother of-David.

**21:22** These four were-born to-the-Rafah in-Gat, and-they-fell by-[the]-hand of-David and-by-[the]-hand of-his-servants.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — beit ha-damim:** Literally "house of the bloods," meaning "the bloodstained house" — a household guilty of bloodshed. The plural *damim* intensifies the guilt.

**v.6 — hoqa'anum:** The verb יקע is debated — "to hang," "to impale," or "to expose (a body)." The exact method of execution is uncertain. It is a ritual act performed "before YHWH," suggesting sacral significance.

**v.8 — Mikhal vs. Merav:** The MT reads "Mikhal" (מיכל), but many scholars and ancient versions read "Merav" (מרב), since Merav was married to Adriel (1 Sam 18:19), not Mikhal. Two Hebrew manuscripts and the LXX read "Merav." The LC text clearly reads מיכל.

**v.10 — Ritspah's vigil:** One of the most haunting images in all of Scripture. Rizpah guards the exposed bodies of her sons from scavenging birds and beasts, from the beginning of barley harvest (April) until the rains come (October) — a vigil of approximately five months.

**v.19 — Elchanan killed Goliath:** This verse presents a famous textual difficulty. The MT says Elhanan killed Goliath the Gittite. The parallel in 1 Chr 20:5 reads "Elhanan son of Jair struck Lahmi the brother of Goliath." The LC text is unambiguous: אֶת־גָּלְיָת.

**v.19 — Ya'arey-Oregim:** The word *oregim* ("weavers") appears to be a scribal duplication from the end of the verse ("like a beam of weavers"). The parallel in Chronicles reads simply "Jair" (יעיר).

*— EMET*
